source_integrity_findings: The Results narrative labels all-but-one (98%) with Borg CR10 <5 as non-COVID-19, while Table 2 shows 41/42 (98%) of the COVID-19 group in the no-dyspnea category; both statements are preserved rather than silently reconciled.

The Results narrative defines “silent hypoxemia” as Borg CR10 ≥5 and reports OR 0.221 (95% CI 0.054-0.907; p=0.036), whereas Table 2 labels Borg ≥5 as dyspnea and reports COVID-19 OR 0.007 (95% CI 0.000-0.199; p=0.004).
The Discussion says COVID-19 patients had a higher dyspnea sensation, conflicting with the abstract, Results, Figure 1, and conclusion indicating lower dyspnea in COVID-19.
schema_gaps: The schema has no native representation for medians with interquartile ranges; medians are stored as estimates and the IQR is preserved in canonical_statement/original_result_text rather than encoded as a confidence interval.
The schema has no explicit field for source-internal contradictions; conflicting reported statements are preserved as separate atoms and reconciled in the validation/processing reports.
extraction_limitations: The article is a five-page retrospective single-center study with no supplements in the packet.
Table 2 analyzes 78 rather than 82 patients, but the source does not explain the four-patient difference or missing-data handling.
Source-internal endpoint/group-label inconsistencies prevent safe normalization of the multivariable “silent hypoxemia” estimate into a single reconciled result.
